criteria.criterion: Every question in quiz.json tests a point about the target of the change that the case brief states
criteria.reason: All 10 questions test points of the brief's target: the result-directory artifact and why it is graded (q1, q6, q10), the check(run) split of engine invariants from behavior rates (q2, q4, q8, q9), the scenario file driving the runner and its extension surface (q5, q7), and the CLI exit codes for trouble kinds (q3, q6, q10).

criteria.criterion: Every question sits at an altitude that the case brief allows, as the brief describes that altitude
criteria.reason: The plan declares altitude 'design', and every question asks why the shape was chosen, what happens on failure, or what extending it touches (problem, shape, alternatives, what it makes easy/hard next), staying above function names and flags; the exit codes and id formats used are the target's own stated vocabulary.

criteria.criterion: No question asks about an incidental part of the change that the case brief lists
criteria.reason: No question addresses the brief's listed incidentals (test fixtures under test/scenarios/plugins, package.json script names, the boundary test edit); every question concerns the runner, the scenario format, the judge, or the CLI.

criteria.criterion: Every wrong option of a single or multi question is a plausible misreading of the change, not filler
criteria.reason: Each distractor encodes a believable misconception: secrecy as the reason for file grading, cheap-checks-first, abort-as-caller-success, invariant-as-advisory, throw-escapes-as-runner-failure, retry logic, skips-count-as-misses, values-only scrubbing - all plausible misreadings, none filler.

criteria.criterion: Each question's key_points state what a correct answer must cover, at the same altitude as the question
criteria.reason: Key points enumerate exactly what a correct answer must cover at each question's own level: q3's code meanings and precedence, q6's failure entry plus kept partial results plus exit 3, q10's directory contents, complete=false, skip reasons, and exit code; q7's key points match its where-does-it-go extension demand.

criteria.criterion: The questions go outside in: the first ones cover what the change is for and its main boundary, narrower mechanisms and details come later, and no question is more central to the change than one asked before it, except the last
criteria.reason: q1 and q2 open with the change's purpose and main boundary, q3 covers the CLI surface, then mechanisms and failure handling (q4-q6), the extension (q7), and narrower details (q8, q9), with the synthesis last; the core/important labels are non-increasing and no later question outranks an earlier one.

criteria.criterion: When quiz.json has two or more questions, the last one applies several points of the change to one new case the change does not spell out
criteria.reason: The last question (q10) applies several points of the change - partial result directory, complete=false, behavior skips with named reasons for steps 2 and 3, and exit code 3 - to one novel case (an overnight provider outage on step 2 of a four-step scenario) the change does not spell out.

criteria.criterion: Every question can be answered by a person who understands what the change does and why, with the code closed: no question depends on recalling a function name, a file name, a flag, an exit code, or an exact value, unless that name or value is itself the point the author must own
criteria.reason: Questions are answerable from understanding with the code closed: options describe behavior rather than hinge on name recall, and the few exact names/values used (exit codes, the [LEAKED:NAME] mark, the name@step report id, the module locations in q7's where-does-it-go) are themselves points the author must own.

criteria.criterion: Every prompt, option, and key point is plain English: short sentences, common words, one idea each, with no jargon the question does not need and no filler or marketing words
criteria.reason: Prompts, options, and key points are short, concrete, common-word sentences, one idea each; terms like invariant, behavior, result directory, and the mark are vocabulary the questions need, and there is no filler or marketing language.
